ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, counterparties, banks, and material suppliers against applicable UN Security Council lists, European Union financial sanctions, French national sanctions, and relevant United States OFAC lists where there is a US nexus. Perform PEP and close-associate screening under Articles L.561-10 and L.561-10-2 of the Code monétaire et financier, apply enhanced due diligence to foreign and domestic PEPs, establish source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, document ownership and control through every intermediate entity, and retain AML records for the statutory retention period. OFAC is not universally binding on a non-US French entity but creates material secondary-sanctions, banking, correspondent, and payment-risk exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the French incorporation documents and registry filing. French law does not generally require a French-language name, but the name must use permitted characters, must not mislead the public, and must comply with public-order, corporate-form, intellectual-property, and regulated-activity restrictions. A SAS name must not create confusion with an existing corporate name, trade name, trademark, or protected designation. Foreign scripts and transliterations should be accompanied by a Latin-script version accepted by the filing system and banks. A prior INPI trademark and corporate-name search is strongly required; registry acceptance does not confer broad trademark protection.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a regulated financial, banking, insurance, investment, payment, or credit activity without the required authorization
Terms suggesting public authority, government status, diplomatic status, or an official European Union or French institution
Protected professional designations and regulated-sector terms used without the applicable authorization
Words or expressions contrary to law, public order, morality, or the rights of third parties
Names confusingly similar to an existing registered company, trade name, trademark, domain name, or protected geographical designation
The words "Société Anonyme" or other corporate-form descriptions where their use would be misleading
Geographical, national, or international institutional references requiring authorization or likely to imply an official affiliation
Agricultural, engineering, construction, certification, or technical-assurance terms that imply qualifications, accreditation, or statutory status not held by the company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation procedure with a universally applicable 30-day reservation period; the 30-day value is an administrative planning window only. Conduct INPI trademark, company-name, trade-name, domain-name, and sanctions screening before filing. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the name, obtain the electronic rejection notice and stated legal ground, correct the filing or propose an alternative name, and resubmit through the portal. Where an appealable administrative decision is issued, file a reasoned administrative reconsideration request with the competent authority and, if necessary, a judicial challenge before the competent French administrative or commercial court within the applicable statutory time limit. A trademark opposition, infringement dispute, or unfair-competition dispute must be pursued separately before the competent court or INPI procedure. No filing should use a name that is merely accepted technically but remains exposed to third-party IP claims.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France under the French Commercial Code. Domiciliation at the representative's premises, at a qualifying domiciliation company, or at premises made available under a valid lease or occupancy arrangement may be permissible, subject to statutory conditions and domiciliation-provider licensing requirements. A virtual office may support incorporation and administrative receipt of correspondence, but it is not a substitute for operational substance where the company performs agricultural-silo EPC, reinforced-concrete construction, engineering coordination, procurement, site supervision, or contracting activities. The company should maintain appropriate personnel, project records, accounting records, safety documentation, insurance, subcontractor controls, and accessible commercial premises or project facilities. Construction activities may require project-specific planning approvals, site authorizations, professional qualifications, ten-year liability insurance, civil liability insurance, health and safety compliance, and public-procurement qualifications even though no single general incorporation license is assumed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official France-wide probability is published. For a newly incorporated SAS conducting ordinary private-sector construction and maintaining a credible French registered office, the estimated risk of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months is low, approximately 1%-5%. The risk may become moderate or high where there are VAT or payroll anomalies, repeated registered-mail failures, a high-risk foreign ownership chain, sanctions or PEP alerts, inconsistent beneficial-owner filings, public procurement, employment or construction-site safety issues, suspected fictitious domiciliation, or tax-residence and substance discrepancies. This is a compliance risk estimate, not a statutory probability.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), under the Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; tax services and online procedures are available through impots.gouv.fr. The Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) handles applicable French tax registrations for non-established businesses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated French SAS obtains a SIREN and SIRET through registration in the Registre national des entreprises, managed by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), via the formalités d’entreprises portal. The DGFiP assigns or confirms the French tax account identifiers. For VAT, the business requests registration from the competent Service des impôts des entreprises and receives a French VAT number in the format FR plus a two-character key and the SIREN. A foreign company making taxable supplies in France without a French establishment generally applies to the SIEE, providing incorporation and tax-residence evidence, identification of its legal representative, activity and transaction details, and, where required, a fiscal representative. EU-established applicants are generally not required to appoint a fiscal representative; non-EU applicants generally must appoint a representative unless an applicable legal exception or mutual assistance arrangement removes that requirement. VAT registration does not itself establish a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying young company may elect, subject to statutory ownership, age, activity, size and other conditions, for temporary taxation under the income-tax regime for up to five fiscal years. This is not a US-style check-the-box election. No general entity-classification election is available to elect pass-through treatment, and no general French hybrid-mismatch election changes the SAS's default classification. Specific tax regimes and treaty relief may apply where statutory conditions are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to a business required to register for VAT on taxable transactions in France. A qualifying small business may use the franchise en base de TVA, subject to current statutory turnover limits and eligibility conditions. For ordinary services, the principal domestic threshold is EUR 37,500, with a higher tolerance threshold; for goods, the principal threshold is EUR 85,000, also with a higher tolerance threshold. Thresholds, transitional rules and eligibility should be confirmed for the relevant tax year. A foreign supplier's registration obligations depend on establishment, transaction type, customer status and applicable reverse-charge or special-scheme rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions between businesses subject to French VAT, with phased requirements beginning in September 2026 and later phases for smaller businesses. In-scope invoices are to be transmitted through an approved platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire) or the public invoicing portal where available; transaction and payment data reporting (e-reporting) applies to specified transactions outside the domestic e-invoicing scope. The regime is not a general real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping system. Public-sector invoicing is handled through Chorus Pro. Businesses should verify the applicable rollout date, platform requirements and transaction coverage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with a right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory conditions are met and the exporter can prove the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be exempt only when the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are transported there, and reporting and documentary conditions are satisfied. Services are not zero-rated merely because the customer or payment is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. A French construction or installation project may be taxable in France, including under special immovable-property rules, regardless of the customer's location. Refunds require valid supporting records and compliance with VAT return and reporting obligations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and electronic exit confirmation or equivalent evidence accepted by the tax authorities
Commercial invoice, sales contract or purchase order identifying the goods, parties, destination and transaction
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as bill of lading, CMR consignment note, air waybill or carrier confirmation
Evidence linking the exported goods to the invoice and customs declaration, including packing lists where relevant
For intra-EU supplies rather than exports outside the EU: customer VAT identification evidence, transport evidence, and required recapitulative and statistical reporting records
Bank remittance evidence may support the audit trail but is not, by itself, a general statutory condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Incorrectly exempted or zero-rated supplies may result in assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest and tax penalties. Penalties depend on the facts and applicable Tax Code provisions; deliberate fraud or fraudulent documentation can trigger materially higher penalties and, where statutory elements are met, criminal proceedings. Input VAT refunds may be denied or recovered if entitlement or supporting evidence is insufficient. Exporters should retain transaction, customs, transport, accounting and VAT records for the applicable statutory retention and limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank for euro monetary policy and payment-system oversight; Banque de France for French banking supervision functions delegated by the European Central Bank, foreign-exchange statistics, balance-of-payments reporting, and national payment-system responsibilities; the French Treasury Directorate-General (Direction générale du Trésor) for financial sanctions and certain national financial-control measures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and generally has full current-account and capital-account convertibility within the European Union framework. A French SAS may receive and remit dividends, interest, principal, service fees, royalties, and capital proceeds cross-border without a general foreign-exchange approval or mandatory conversion into euros. Transfers remain subject to bank AML and counter-terrorist-financing controls, beneficial-owner identification, sanctions screening, tax compliance, transfer-pricing support, corporate-authority evidence, and applicable reporting. Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, restricted counterparties, unusual third-party accounts, cash-intensive structures, or unsupported intercompany balances may be delayed, rejected, frozen, or reported. Dividend and interest remittances require available distributable profits or valid debt documentation, corporate approvals, withholding-tax analysis, and applicable treaty or European Union directive relief. Cross-border cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more carried by individuals are subject to customs declaration requirements; this does not constitute a general restriction on bank transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, convert a prescribed percentage of export receipts into euros, or repatriate export proceeds within a fixed foreign-exchange deadline. Export proceeds may ordinarily remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through foreign or French accounts, subject to contractual banking requirements, accounting records, tax documentation, sanctions controls, and applicable statistical or payment-reporting obligations. Customs export formalities and VAT evidence must be maintained separately from foreign-exchange controls. Banks may impose internal receipt, documentary, or transaction-monitoring deadlines under their account terms and AML procedures; those contractual controls are not statutory surrender ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment operations and low to medium as a substitute for a French domestic bank. A licensed European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarding, SEPA transfers, foreign-currency services, and, where authorized, cross-border payment services. An offshore digital EMI without European authorization, passporting, or a properly appointed European service structure cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services in France merely through an online interface. An EMI account should not be assumed to satisfy French share-capital escrow, notarial capital-deposit, local bank-account, lender, or major-customer requirements. EMI onboarding remains subject to AML, UBO, source-of-funds, sanctions, transaction-purpose, and geographic-risk controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal French statutory requirement for all directors to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or reliable electronic identification, certified corporate documents, video verification, and verified beneficial-owner information. In practice, a bank may require a director, legal representative, UBO, or authorized signatory to attend a video or in-person interview, particularly where the SAS is newly incorporated, foreign-owned, construction-sector payments are international, ownership is layered, the registered office is serviced, or expected transaction volumes are high. Capital escrow availability and final operational-account activation are bank-specific and may require original, apostilled, legalized, translated, or independently verified documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with no operating history, no completed French annual accounts, or no demonstrated commercial activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; statutes; certificate of incorporation; proof of registered office; board or shareholder resolutions; business plan; project pipeline; signed or draft EPC contracts; expected-account-activity schedule; first-year budget; tax-registration evidence; and identification of all directors, authorized signatories, and UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership, nominee arrangements, multi-layer holding companies, trusts, or inability to identify the natural-person UBO.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart to natural persons; registers of shareholders and directors; certificates of incorporation and good standing for each entity; constitutional documents; trust or foundation instruments where applicable; UBO declarations; passports and residential-address evidence; and a written ownership-purpose memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from a shareholder or group company with an unclear purpose, inconsistent amount, or unsupported source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder-loan or equity-subscription documents; capital-increase or contribution resolutions; investor bank statements; audited accounts; sale or financing agreements; proof of source of wealth and source of funds; transfer instructions stating the correct economic purpose; and tax and accounting treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Construction-sector payments involving project advances, subcontractors, brokers, public-sector counterparties, or high-value cross-border transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tender or contract package; customer and subcontractor due-diligence files; beneficial-owner checks; invoices; purchase orders; delivery or progress certificates; project-country analysis; sanctions screening results; anti-bribery policy; payment-approval matrix; and reconciliation between invoices, milestones, and bank transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments, payments from an account in a different jurisdiction, or requests to remit funds to an unrelated beneficiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Triangular-payment explanation; contractual payment clause; written authorization from the contracting party; relationship and UBO evidence for each party; invoice and settlement statement; sanctions screening; bank confirmation of account ownership; and documented management approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity materially exceeds the profile declared at onboarding or includes currencies and countries not reflected in the business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated rolling cash-flow forecast; project-by-project transaction map; customer and supplier list; forecast currency exposures; revised account-activity profile; supporting contracts; treasury policy; and management explanation of the variance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete beneficial-owner information, expired identification documents, inconsistent corporate data, or inability to verify the registered office.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract; certified corporate register documents; valid identification; proof of residential address; lease or domiciliation agreement; utility or tax evidence; translated and legalized foreign documents where requested; and a single controlled data room containing consistent records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions, export-control, dual-use, corruption, or politically exposed-person exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening report; counterparties' ownership and control analysis; end-use and end-user statements; export-control classification; anti-corruption due diligence; country-risk memorandum; compliance approvals; and escalation records for any potential match.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cash, virtual assets, unregulated payment intermediaries, or anonymous funding channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition or risk-acceptance policy; full banking trail; independently verifiable source-of-funds records; regulated-intermediary confirmations; transaction reconciliation; and a remediation plan demonstrating that future payments will use regulated accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a designated French bank capital escrow account when required for the incorporation or capital increase, with the transfer sent from the investor's account and a payment reference identifying the SAS, subscription or contribution purpose, and relevant corporate resolution. For shareholder loans or other intercompany funding, use a documented loan or financing agreement, transfer-pricing support, maturity and interest terms, lender UBO evidence, and a purpose reference consistent with the legal instrument. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border payments for non-SEPA or non-euro transfers; ISO 20022 payment messages are increasingly standard, although banks may still describe legacy correspondent instructions using MT terminology. Verify beneficiary name, IBAN, BIC, intermediary-bank requirements, sanctions status, source of funds, and receipt against the general ledger. Retain bank advices, contracts, resolutions, subscription records, and accounting evidence. Do not route capital through personal accounts or unrelated third parties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and bank-to-bank SWIFT transfers for non-SEPA or foreign-currency settlements. A SWIFT MT103 is a legacy customer-credit-transfer format; the applicable bank may process the same payment through ISO 20022 pacs.008 or another current message standard. For milestone EPC payments, require an executed contract, invoice, approved progress or delivery certificate, purchase order, beneficiary-account verification, sanctions screening, and dual authorization. For documentary trade or project financing, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit, standby letter of credit, or demand guarantee through the bank's trade-finance desk, with clearly defined Incoterms, documents required for presentation, expiry, latest shipment or performance dates, discrepancy rules, and UCP 600 or ISP98 rules as applicable. Construction milestones should be supported by engineer, architect, customer, or independent-certifier evidence where contractually required. Monitor withholding tax, VAT, subcontractor reporting, anti-bribery, export-control, and foreign-exchange documentation before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm, supported by a documented underlying exposure, treasury policy, counterparty limit, confirmation, valuation, and settlement instructions.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, product, counterparty, and jurisdiction are legally permitted; settlement is normally in a specified convertible currency against an agreed fixing, and the transaction remains subject to bank eligibility, derivatives documentation, EMIR, MiFID II, sanctions, and reporting requirements.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring or long-dated funding and cash-flow exposures, subject to appropriate ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation, close-out, accounting, and EMIR obligations.

Foreign-exchange options and collars may be available for eligible corporate clients, subject to suitability or appropriateness assessment, product disclosure, premium or collateral requirements, and documented risk limits.

Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion, subject to ordinary payment screening and transaction documentation. Hedging should not be used for unsupported speculation, and the SAS should reconcile each derivative to a documented receivable, payable, debt service, forecast transaction, or committed project exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Bilan and Compte de Résultat) with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 7,500 EUR; risk of company strike-off for non-compliance after 3 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after financial year-end or upon any change in UBO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR; potential penalties for non-declaration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if annual turnover exceeds 50 million EUR, balance sheet total exceeds 43 million EUR, or average number of employees exceeds 500
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) for most SAS entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration of UBOs to the French tax authorities within 3 months of year-end; register must be maintained at registered office
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registre des mandataires sociaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-12,000 USD depending on audit threshold compliance

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A 3.3% social contribution may apply to companies with turnover of at least EUR 7.63 million and corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000, producing an aggregate effective rate of approximately 25.83%, subject to statutory conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may obtain a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, capital is fully paid up, and at least 75% of the share capital is held by individuals or qualifying companies. New businesses may qualify for sector- and location-specific incentives. Research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to qualifying conditions. Certain intellectual-property income may qualify for a 10% rate under the French patent box regime. Tax holidays are not generally available solely because the SAS performs silo or elevator construction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited under French law; the specified five-year limit does not apply. Utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million in the relevant year. Tax losses may generally be carried back to the preceding financial year, subject to an election and a EUR 1 million cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account using EFI or an accredited EDI provider. The 2065 return is accompanied by the relevant annual tax package, including Forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and balance-sheet and profit-and-loss schedules 2050-SD through 2057-SD, as applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with corporate income tax instalments generally payable quarterly and a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the electronic return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For a non-calendar year-end, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the applicable payment calendar and electronic-payment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, financial year dates, legal form, and principal business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the French SAS as the taxpayer. The French SAS must report its French legal identity, SIREN, French registered office, and French tax office. The foreign parent is disclosed only where requested for ownership, related-party, or withholding-tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable result and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, provisions, participation exemptions, foreign taxes, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the French SAS's worldwide taxable result, subject to French exemptions and foreign-tax relief rules. Do not deduct shareholder-level costs merely because they were incurred by a foreign parent. Related-party charges must satisfy benefit, arm's-length, documentation, and withholding requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-A-SD, reconciliation of accounting result to taxable result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling statutory accounts to the French tax result, including non-deductible penalties, excess interest, provisions, depreciation adjustments, tax credits, and exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign accounting classifications must be mapped to French tax categories. Construction contract revenue, retention amounts, work-in-progress, contract costs, provisions, and completion adjustments must be supported by project-level records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses utilized during the year, losses generated during the year, and remaining losses available for future periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Track French tax losses separately from foreign parent losses. A substantial change in business activity, including a genuine transformation of the business, may restrict or eliminate the right to use historical losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, allocation of profit and distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit allocation, reserves, retained earnings, dividends, and other distributions or deemed distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributions to a foreign shareholder must be reconciled with French withholding-tax reporting, treaty relief, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where applicable, and corporate-law approval of the accounts and dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2059-B-SD and 2059-C-SD, capital gains and special tax items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals, long-term capital gains, depreciable assets, and relevant special regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disposals of French business assets, shares, or real estate interests must be reviewed for French taxation, treaty allocation, real-estate withholding, and anti-abuse provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, liabilities, and related accounting disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts must agree with the approved French statutory accounts. Intercompany balances must identify counterparties, currency, maturity, interest terms, and settlement status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure and supporting documentation for controlled transactions, including management fees, royalties, financing, guarantees, procurement, and cost allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the benefit received by the SAS, allocation keys, pricing methodology, contractual basis, evidence of services, and withholding-tax treatment. Payments to low-tax or non-cooperative jurisdictions require heightened review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Corporate income tax instalments and final balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly instalments and the final settlement calculated from the filed liability, with electronic payment through the professional tax account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder cannot generally pay French corporate income tax through its own foreign return. The French SAS must maintain its own French tax account and payment mandate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased penalties for formal notices, opposition to tax audits, or fraudulent conduct. Late payment interest is generally 0.20% per month under Article 1727 of the French Tax Code. Deliberate inaccuracies may attract a 40% penalty; fraudulent conduct, abuse of law, or certain obstruction may attract an 80% penalty. Additional penalties may apply for omitted disclosures, undeclared foreign accounts, late withholding filings, and failure to submit required transfer-pricing or country-by-country information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Forms 2571-SD, 2572-SD, and related corporate income tax payment references, filed or paid electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account. Withholding returns may use Forms 2777-SD and relevant dividend, interest, and royalty reporting forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly or annual depending on the tax and payment category; corporate income tax instalments are generally quarterly, while withholding obligations arise when the relevant payment is made.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on specified quarterly dates, with the final balance generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end. Dividend, interest, and royalty withholding is generally declared and paid by the 15th day of the month following the payment or distribution, subject to the applicable form and payment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD, final corporate income tax balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross annual corporate income tax liability, instalments already paid, tax credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065 and the general ledger. Foreign tax credits and French tax credits must be supported by statutory certificates and must not be claimed twice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross distributions or payments, applicable withholding rate, treaty or directive exemption, amount withheld, and payment date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the beneficial owner, residence jurisdiction, treaty article, residence certificate, shareholding percentage, holding period, and anti-abuse analysis. Apply the domestic rate where relief-at-source conditions are not satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late withholding returns or payment may trigger a 5% surcharge for late payment in specified circumstances, a 10% or higher filing penalty depending on the default and notice status, 0.20% monthly interest, and the withholding tax itself. Incorrectly applying treaty relief may result in recovery from the French payer, penalties, and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident legal entity, the domestic withholding rate is generally 25%, subject to applicable exemptions and tax treaties. A 0% exemption may apply under the French implementation of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring an eligible EU or EEA parent, a minimum 10% holding, a minimum two-year holding commitment, subject-to-tax and beneficial-ownership conditions, and anti-abuse compliance. Different domestic rules apply to individual recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and complete the applicable French treaty forms, commonly Form 5000 and the relevant dividend, interest, or royalty annex such as Form 5001, 5002, or 5003. The French payer should retain the forms, verify beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, legal ownership, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose concerns, and anti-conduit indicators. If relief at source is unavailable, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund through the French tax administration using the prescribed forms. Treaty relief is not automatic merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 25% under Article 182 B of the French Tax Code, subject to treaty reduction, EU directive relief, beneficial-ownership requirements, and anti-abuse rules. French domestic withholding on ordinary interest paid to a non-resident is generally 0%, but exceptions can apply, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, certain profit-participating or hybrid instruments, and specific statutory anti-abuse provisions. Treaty rates vary by treaty and commonly range from 0% to 15% for royalties and from 0% to 15% for interest. The payer must review interest limitation, recharacterization, beneficial ownership, hybrid mismatch, thin capitalization, and principal-purpose issues.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million of annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets generally triggers the full French transfer-pricing documentation obligation, including a Local File and Master File under Articles L13 AA and L13 AB of the French Tax Procedures Code. A Country-by-Country Report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Separate transfer-pricing disclosure and summary requirements may apply below the full-documentation threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to a generalized ESR statute. Substance is enforced through the French general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, principal-purpose analysis under treaties, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, hybrid mismatch rules, anti-conduit principles, and EU anti-avoidance legislation. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, personnel or genuinely outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure, project-management evidence, contracting authority, risk control, bank-account functionality, accounting records, and commercial rationale proportionate to its construction activities. A French company with no personnel, no operational control, circular funds, and pass-through invoices faces heightened recharacterization and permanent-establishment risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.construction_sector_transfer_pricing_con: For EPC and agricultural-silo projects, preserve bids, tender documents, bills of quantities, subcontractor agreements, engineering deliverables, milestone certificates, variation orders, retention calculations, warranty obligations, insurance, site records, cost-to-complete calculations, and allocation keys. Related-party engineering, procurement, financing, guarantee, management, and intellectual-property charges must be separately analyzed. Low-risk routine service characterization is not appropriate if the SAS controls construction execution, bears performance risk, provides warranties, owns customer relationships, or assumes significant project or site risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing revenue, inflating subcontractor costs, creating false invoices, omitting taxable distributions, falsifying project costs, or using sham intercompany charges to reduce French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may reach 40% for deliberate conduct and 80% for fraudulent conduct, abuse of law, or certain obstruction, in addition to tax recovery and 0.20% monthly interest. Criminal tax fraud may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, increased in aggravated cases to up to seven years and EUR 3 million, with higher penalties linked to proceeds or specific circumstances. Corporate criminal fines may be multiplied by five.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, and civil tax liability where they personally participated or committed serious and repeated tax misconduct. A director may also be declared jointly liable for tax debts in cases of fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated failure under French tax law. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered by a court in appropriate criminal proceedings; veil piercing is exceptional and fact-dependent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, fictitious subcontracting, and accounting fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for work not performed, routing payments through undisclosed intermediaries, recycling invoices, falsifying completion certificates, or recording personal expenditure as construction cost.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions and tax credits, 40% or 80% tax penalties, recovery of unpaid withholding and VAT, and potential criminal prosecution for forgery, use of forged documents, fraud, or tax fraud. Criminal sanctions depend on the offense and facts and may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and corporate fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or knowingly tolerate false documentation may incur criminal and civil liability. A director may be barred from management, required to contribute to an insolvency shortfall in cases of management fault, and exposed to personal tax liability under the relevant statutory conditions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to charge or report French VAT, claiming input VAT on fictitious invoices, misclassifying construction services, using foreign entities to disguise a French place of supply, or participating in carousel or missing-trader arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of VAT, late-payment interest, 40% or 80% penalties, and criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud. VAT invoices must reflect the actual supplier, customer, place of supply, reverse-charge status, and taxable amount. Intra-EU reporting failures may create separate penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors may face criminal sanctions, personal tax liability for fraudulent or repeated conduct, management bans, asset confiscation, and insolvency-related liability. The French tax authority may deny input VAT where the company knew or should have known that the transaction formed part of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive foreign management fees, unsupported royalties, interest-free or non-commercial loans, guarantees without remuneration, artificial cost allocations, or shifting construction profits to a low-tax affiliate without corresponding functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust taxable profit under the arm's-length principle, impose 40% or 80% penalties where appropriate, charge interest, apply withholding tax to recharacterized distributions or royalties, and impose documentation-related penalties. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation can trigger a specific penalty generally based on the greater of a statutory minimum or 0.5% of the transactions lacking documentation, subject to applicable limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed where they knowingly approve non-arm's-length arrangements, conceal records, or obstruct an audit. Personal liability is not automatic for an ordinary pricing error but may arise from fraud, serious management fault, or deliberate tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper treaty or EU withholding-tax relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a 0% or reduced rate without a valid residence certificate, paying a conduit entity, ignoring beneficial-ownership defects, backdating treaty forms, or using an interposed holding company with no commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and penalties. Anti-abuse provisions may deny treaty or EU directive relief and recharacterize payments as taxable distributions, interest, royalties, or hidden distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving knowingly incorrect withholding treatment may face civil, administrative, and criminal consequences depending on intent. The payer's legal representative can be pursued for compliance failures, particularly where records were falsified or the arrangement was deliberately abusive.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, hidden beneficial ownership, and unlawful profit diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS as a nominee or pass-through entity, concealing the beneficial owner, using nominee directors, circularly transferring project receipts, or diverting company assets for shareholder benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include tax reassessment, abuse-of-law treatment, confiscation, money-laundering prosecution, corporate dissolution in severe cases, and penalties for inaccurate beneficial-owner filings. French companies must maintain and report beneficial-owner information to the competent registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability for concealment, misuse of corporate assets, money laundering, or fraudulent management. Management bans, asset confiscation, civil restitution, insolvency contribution claims, and imprisonment may apply. Travel bans require a specific judicial order and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or third-party payments, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions or adverse media, processing suspicious milestone payments, or failing to report suspicious transactions where a regulated professional obligation applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated cases carrying up to ten years and a EUR 750,000 fine. Legal entities may face fines multiplied by five, confiscation, and additional measures. AML-regulated professionals may face supervisory sanctions, fines, and restrictions for customer-due-diligence failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate in laundering may be imprisoned, fined, disqualified, and subjected to confiscation. Directors may also face civil and regulatory liability for systemic AML failures. Suspicious transaction reporting obligations depend on whether the SAS or its professional advisers fall within the regulated perimeter.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bribery, public procurement corruption, and facilitation payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying commissions to obtain public or private construction contracts, disguising bribes as consultancy or success fees, offering benefits to inspectors, or manipulating tender processes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Active or passive bribery may result in imprisonment and substantial fines, including corporate fines that can reach EUR 5 million or twice the proceeds for certain offenses. Additional confiscation, exclusion from public procurement, and compliance-program measures may apply. Sapin II compliance duties may apply to qualifying companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may face imprisonment, fines, professional disqualification, confiscation, and civil restitution. Directors can be liable for authorizing or concealing bribery even where the payment was made through an intermediary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared work and construction labor violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undeclared workers, bogus self-employed subcontractors, undocumented labor, false subcontractor certificates, or labor-only subcontracting designed to avoid payroll charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Undeclared work can trigger social-security reassessment, cancellation of exemptions, administrative fines, criminal penalties, and exclusion from public procurement. Individual penalties can include up to three years' imprisonment and a EUR 45,000 fine, with higher sanctions in aggravated circumstances; corporate fines may be multiplied by five. Construction-specific obligations include verification of subcontractor compliance and, where relevant, site documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally, fined, imprisoned, disqualified, and held liable for social-security or insolvency consequences where they knowingly organize or tolerate undeclared work.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting, statutory audit, and corporate-law failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to keep French accounting records, manipulating annual accounts, distributing dividends from fictitious profits, failing to appoint a statutory auditor when required, or withholding financial information from shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible consequences include refusal of tax deductions, administrative and criminal sanctions for false accounts, invalid or unlawful distributions, shareholder claims, auditor reporting, and management bans. Unlawful dividends may have to be repaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors may incur civil liability for mismanagement, repayment of unlawful distributions, contribution to insolvency liabilities, and criminal liability for false accounts or misuse of corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ignoring mandatory health and safety controls, causing serious worker injury through negligent management, mishandling asbestos or hazardous materials, or breaching environmental and waste requirements at silo construction sites.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions may include criminal fines, imprisonment for individuals in serious cases, administrative orders, work stoppage, remediation costs, environmental fines, loss of permits or procurement eligibility, and civil damages. Liability depends on the specific labor, environmental, planning, and safety offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, site managers, and responsible officers may face personal criminal and civil liability for intentional or negligent breaches, including bodily injury or environmental damage. Corporate limited liability does not protect individuals from their own offenses.
